name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

description: "How to drive the real built JusPrin app for a screenshot-per-step UX walkthrough (2026-10-28): scratch copies, the empty local_machines loop with the fake printer, why background app_* tools fail on Orca dialogs, and where screenshots land."

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].

`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

description: "How to drive the real built JusPrin app for a screenshot-per-step UX walkthrough (2026-10-28): scratch copies, the empty local_machines loop with the fake printer, why background app_* tools fail on Orca dialogs, and where screenshots land."

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].

import json

from django.conf import settings
from django.http import HttpResponse, JsonResponse
from django.shortcuts import render
from django.utils import timezone
from django.views.decorators.csrf import csrf_exempt
from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET, require_POST
from lib.file_storage import save_file_obj
from PIL import Image, UnidentifiedImageError

from jusprin.ledger.account import account as account_summary
from jusprin.ledger.ledger import ensure_lots
from jusprin.ledger.models import PrintReport
from jusprin.ledger.reports import ReportRefused, is_reported, submit_report

from .aliases import get_aliases
from .auth import authenticate
from .errors import error_body


@require_GET
def models(request):
    """The aliases this person can pick, in display order. "format" is the
    backend the person is currently assigned for the alias, and so the
    endpoint the client should use for a new chat."""
    user = authenticate(request)
    if user is None:
        return HttpResponse(error_body('unauthorized'), status=401, content_type='application/json')
    ensure_lots(user.id)
    data = [{
        'id': alias.id,
        'label': alias.label,
        'format': alias.group_for(user.id).format,
        'efforts': list(alias.efforts),
        # Left out when there is none: released apps read it as a string.
        **({'default_effort': alias.default_effort} if alias.default_effort else {}),
        'tier': alias.tier,
        'credits': alias.credits,
        'images': alias.backends[alias.group_for(user.id).format].images,
    } for alias in get_aliases().values()]
    response = JsonResponse({'data': data})
    response['Cache-Control'] = 'no-store'
    return response


@require_GET
def account(request):
    """The person's credits, plan and usage, for the composer's balance ring and
    the pre-send check."""
    user = authenticate(request)
    if user is None:
        return HttpResponse(error_body('unauthorized'), status=401, content_type='application/json')
    response = JsonResponse(account_summary(user))
    response['Cache-Control'] = 'no-store'
    return response


# Where the desktop app's loopback server sends the browser after it finishes,
# or fails, the OAuth code exchange.
@require_GET
def signed_in(request):
    return render(request, 'jusprin/v2/sign_in_result.html', {
        'heading': "You're signed in to JusPrin",
        'line': 'You can close this tab and go back to JusPrin.',
    })


@require_GET
def sign_in_failed(request):
    return render(request, 'jusprin/v2/sign_in_result.html', {
        'heading': "Signing in didn't finish",
        'line': 'Go back to JusPrin and try again.',
    })


def _refuse(code: str, status: int) -> HttpResponse:
    return HttpResponse(error_body(code), status=status, content_type='application/json')


def _decodable(photo) -> bool:
    try:
        with Image.open(photo) as image:
            image.verify()
        return True
    except (UnidentifiedImageError, OSError, SyntaxError, Image.DecompressionBombError):
        return False
    finally:
        photo.seek(0)


def _store_photos(user, gcode_hash: str, photos) -> list:
    stamp = str(timezone.now().timestamp())
    urls = []
    for index, photo in enumerate(photos):
        path = f'print_reports/{user.id}/{gcode_hash}/{stamp}_{index}'
        _, url = save_file_obj(path, photo, settings.TIMELAPSE_CONTAINER, user.syndicate.name, long_term_storage=True)
        urls.append(url)
    return urls


@csrf_exempt
@require_POST
def print_reports(request):
    """A person's report on how a print came out. Multipart: gcode_hash, outcome,
    text, facts (a JSON object) and one or more photos."""
    user = authenticate(request)
    if user is None:
        return _refuse('unauthorized', 401)
    gcode_hash = request.POST.get('gcode_hash', '').strip()
    outcome = request.POST.get('outcome', '')
    text = request.POST.get('text', '').strip()
    try:
        facts = json.loads(request.POST.get('facts', '{}'))
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return _refuse('invalid_request', 400)
    if not gcode_hash or outcome not in dict(PrintReport.OUTCOMES) or not isinstance(facts, dict):
        return _refuse('invalid_request', 400)
    if len(text) < settings.JUSPRIN_V2_REPORT_MIN_TEXT:
        return _refuse('text_too_short', 400)
    photos = request.FILES.getlist('photos')
    if not photos:
        return _refuse('photo_needed', 400)
    if len(photos) > settings.JUSPRIN_V2_REPORT_MAX_PHOTOS or any(photo.size > settings.JUSPRIN_V2_REPORT_MAX_PHOTO_BYTES for photo in photos):
        return _refuse('request_too_large', 413)
    if not all(_decodable(photo) for photo in photos):
        return _refuse('photo_unreadable', 400)

@require_GET
def models(request):
    """The aliases this person can pick, in display order. "format" is the
    backend the person is currently assigned for the alias, and so the
    endpoint the client should use for a new chat."""
    user = authenticate(request)
    if user is None:
        return HttpResponse(error_body('unauthorized'), status=401, content_type='application/json')
    ensure_lots(user.id)
    data = [{
        'id': alias.id,
        'label': alias.label,
        'format': alias.group_for(user.id).format,
        'efforts': list(alias.efforts),
        # Left out when there is none: released apps read it as a string.
        **({'default_effort': alias.default_effort} if alias.default_effort else {}),
        'tier': alias.tier,
        'credits': alias.credits,
        'images': alias.backends[alias.group_for(user.id).format].images,
    } for alias in get_aliases().values()]
    response = JsonResponse({'data': data})
    response['Cache-Control'] = 'no-store'
    return response


@require_GET
def account(request):
    """The person's credits, plan and usage, for the composer's balance ring and
    the pre-send check."""
    user = authenticate(request)
    if user is None:
        return HttpResponse(error_body('unauthorized'), status=401, content_type='application/json')
    response = JsonResponse(account_summary(user))
    response['Cache-Control'] = 'no-store'
    return response

        'heading': "Signing in didn't finish",
        'line': 'Go back to JusPrin and try again.',
    })


def _refuse(code: str, status: int) -> HttpResponse:
    return HttpResponse(error_body(code), status=status, content_type='application/json')


def _decodable(photo) -> bool:
    try:
        with Image.open(photo) as image:
            image.verify()
        return True
    except (UnidentifiedImageError, OSError, SyntaxError, Image.DecompressionBombError):
        return False
    finally:
        photo.seek(0)


def _store_photos(user, gcode_hash: str, photos) -> list:
    stamp = str(timezone.now().timestamp())
    urls = []
    for index, photo in enumerate(photos):
        path = f'print_reports/{user.id}/{gcode_hash}/{stamp}_{index}'
        _, url = save_file_obj(path, photo, settings.TIMELAPSE_CONTAINER, user.syndicate.name, long_term_storage=True)
        urls.append(url)
    return urls

@require_POST
def print_reports(request):
    """A person's report on how a print came out. Multipart: gcode_hash, outcome,
    text, facts (a JSON object) and one or more photos."""
    user = authenticate(request)
    if user is None:
        return _refuse('unauthorized', 401)
    gcode_hash = request.POST.get('gcode_hash', '').strip()
    outcome = request.POST.get('outcome', '')
    text = request.POST.get('text', '').strip()
    try:
        facts = json.loads(request.POST.get('facts', '{}'))
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return _refuse('invalid_request', 400)
    if not gcode_hash or outcome not in dict(PrintReport.OUTCOMES) or not isinstance(facts, dict):
        return _refuse('invalid_request', 400)
    if len(text) < settings.JUSPRIN_V2_REPORT_MIN_TEXT:
        return _refuse('text_too_short', 400)
    photos = request.FILES.getlist('photos')
    if not photos:
        return _refuse('photo_needed', 400)
    if len(photos) > settings.JUSPRIN_V2_REPORT_MAX_PHOTOS or any(photo.size > settings.JUSPRIN_V2_REPORT_MAX_PHOTO_BYTES for photo in photos):
        return _refuse('request_too_large', 413)
    if not all(_decodable(photo) for photo in photos):
        return _refuse('photo_unreadable', 400)

    if is_reported(user, gcode_hash):
        return _refuse('already_reported', 409)
    try:

    except ReportRefused as refused:

    return JsonResponse({'id': report.id, 'credits': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_REPORT_CREDITS,

def add_lot(self, kind, credits, source_ref, expires_at=None):
        return CreditGrant.objects.create(user=self.user, kind=kind, credits_granted=credits,
                                          credits_remaining=credits, source_ref=source_ref,
                                          expires_at=expires_at)

    def left(self, lot):
        lot.refresh_from_db()
        return lot.credits_remaining

    def set_left(self, lot, credits):
        CreditGrant.objects.filter(pk=lot.pk).update(credits_remaining=credits)

    def end_first_month(self):
        CreditGrant.objects.filter(pk=self.signup.pk).update(expires_at=timezone.now() - timedelta(seconds=1))

    def free_lots(self):
        return CreditGrant.objects.filter(user=self.user, kind=CreditGrant.FREE).order_by('id')

    def plan(self, plan_id, **fields):
        JusPrinPlan.objects.update_or_create(user=self.user, defaults={
            'plan_id': plan_id, 'external_id': 'x', 'external_user_id': 'y', **fields})


class FirstContactTests(LedgerTestCase):
    def test_a_pack_holder_gets_free_credits_too(self):
        self.add_lot('pack', 500, 'inv:1')
        self.end_first_month()
        ensure_lots(self.user.id)
        self.assertEqual(self.free_lots().count(), 1)

    def test_a_subscriber_gets_no_free_credits_until_the_plan_lapses(self):
        self.plan('jusprin-hobby-monthly')
        self.end_first_month()
        ensure_lots(self.user.id)
        self.assertEqual(self.free_lots().count(), 0)
        self.plan('jusprin-hobby-monthly', expired_at=timezone.now() - timedelta(days=1))
        ensure_lots(self.user.id)
        self.assertEqual(self.free_lots().count(), 1)

    def test_a_v1_subscriber_gets_the_first_month_credits(self):
        self.plan('jusprin-unlimited-annual')
        ensure_lots(self.user.id)
        signup = CreditGrant.objects.get(user=self.user, kind=CreditGrant.SIGNUP)
        self.assertEqual((signup.credits_granted, signup.credits_remaining), (500, 500))

    def test_a_v1_subscriber_counts_as_subscribed(self):
        self.plan('jusprin-unlimited-annual')
        self.end_first_month()
        ensure_lots(self.user.id)
        self.assertEqual(self.free_lots().count(), 0)

    def test_a_plan_row_we_do_not_sell_is_not_a_subscription(self):
        self.plan('jusprin-free')
        self.end_first_month()
        ensure_lots(self.user.id)
        self.assertEqual(self.free_lots().count(), 1)

    def test_v1_subscribers_are_named_with_the_price_they_keep(self):
        JusPrinPlan.objects.create(user=self.user, plan_id='jusprin-unlimited-annual', external_id='x', external_user_id='y')
        answer = account(self.user)
        self.assertIsNone(answer['plan'])
        self.assertEqual(answer['v1_subscription'], {'plan_id': 'jusprin-unlimited-annual', 'cents': 5999, 'period': 'year'})

    @override_settings(JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES=two_aliases())
    def test_the_endpoints_need_a_token_and_report_prices(self):
        app = Application.objects.create(
            client_id=f'JusPrin2-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}', name='JusPrin 2', client_type=Application.CLIENT_PUBLIC,
            authorization_grant_type=Application.GRANT_AUTHORIZATION_CODE, redirect_uris='http://127.0.0.1/callback')
        token = AccessToken.objects.create(user=self.user, application=app, token=uuid.uuid4().hex, scope='read write',
                                           expires=timezone.now() + timedelta(days=1)).token
        self.assertEqual(Client().get('/ent/jusprin/v2/account').status_code, 401)
        response = Client().get('/ent/jusprin/v2/account', HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f'Bearer {token}')
        self.assertEqual((response.status_code, response['Cache-Control']), (200, 'no-store'))
        self.assertEqual(response.json()['credits']['total'], 500)
        models = Client().get('/ent/jusprin/v2/models', HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f'Bearer {token}').json()['data']
        self.assertEqual([(m['id'], m['tier'], m['credits'], m['images']) for m in models],
                         [('slicer-1', 'expert', 5, True), ('slicer-basic', 'basic', 1, False)])

    def test_a_model_with_no_effort_names_no_default_effort(self):
        # Released apps read default_effort as a string and stop at a null.
        config = json.loads(two_aliases())
        config['aliases'][1].update(efforts=[], default_effort=None)
        config['aliases'][1]['backends']['responses']['effort_map'] = {}
        app = Application.objects.create(
            client_id=f'JusPrin2-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}', name='JusPrin 2', client_type=Application.CLIENT_PUBLIC,
            authorization_grant_type=Application.GRANT_AUTHORIZATION_CODE, redirect_uris='http://127.0.0.1/callback')
        token = AccessToken.objects.create(user=self.user, application=app, token=uuid.uuid4().hex, scope='read write',
                                           expires=timezone.now() + timedelta(days=1)).token
        with override_settings(JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES=json.dumps(config)):
            models = Client().get('/ent/jusprin/v2/models', HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f'Bearer {token}').json()['data']
        standard = next(m for m in models if m['id'] == 'slicer-basic')
        self.assertEqual(standard['efforts'], [])
        self.assertNotIn('default_effort', standard)

"""Charging a turn against a person's lots of credits.

Every credit is the same. A turn costs its alias's price, except a turn the app
started by itself (the file-opened report, the slice-finished note) and a basic
message on an active Workshop plan, which cost nothing.
"""
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Dict, Optional

from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta
from django.conf import settings
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model

class CreditsExhausted(Exception):
    """The next turn cannot be paid."""

    def __init__(self, balance: int, cost: int, plan: Optional[str]):
        super().__init__(f'{cost} credits needed, {balance} available')
        self.balance = balance
        self.cost = cost

"""GET /ent/jusprin/v2/account_box: the launch offer for people who have not
paid, nothing for those who have, and nothing once the offer ends."""
import uuid
from datetime import timedelta

from django.test import Client, TestCase, override_settings
from django.utils import timezone
from oauth2_provider.models import AccessToken, Application

from app.models import User
from jusprin.ledger.models import CreditGrant
from jusprin.models import JusPrinPlan

URL = '/ent/jusprin/v2/account_box'
OFFER = 'Double credits on everything'
SIGN_UP = 'Sign up today. Until 31 Jan, every credit pack and every month of every plan gives twice the credits.'


class AccountBoxTests(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.user = User.objects.create(email=f'box-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com')
        app = Application.objects.create(
            client_id=f'JusPrin2-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}', name='JusPrin 2', client_type=Application.CLIENT_PUBLIC,
            authorization_grant_type=Application.GRANT_AUTHORIZATION_CODE, redirect_uris='http://127.0.0.1/callback')
        self.token = AccessToken.objects.create(user=self.user, application=app, token=uuid.uuid4().hex,
                                                scope='read write', expires=timezone.now() + timedelta(days=1)).token

    def signed_in(self):
        return Client().get(URL, HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f'Bearer {self.token}')

    def grant(self, kind, source_ref):
        CreditGrant.objects.create(user=self.user, kind=kind, credits_granted=500, credits_remaining=0,
                                   source_ref=source_ref, expires_at=timezone.now() - timedelta(days=40))

    def assertNoBox(self, response):
        self.assertEqual((response.status_code, response.content, response['Cache-Control']), (204, b'', 'no-store'))

    def test_signed_out_gets_sign_up_and_the_offer(self):
        response = Client().get(URL)
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual((response['Content-Type'], response['Cache-Control']), ('text/html; charset=utf-8', 'no-store'))
        self.assertContains(response, 'LAUNCH CELEBRATION')
        self.assertContains(response, OFFER)
        self.assertContains(response, SIGN_UP)

    def test_signed_in_never_paid_gets_the_offer_without_sign_up(self):
        response = self.signed_in()
        self.assertContains(response, OFFER)
        self.assertContains(response, 'Until 31 Jan, every credit pack')
        self.assertNotContains(response, 'Sign up')

    def test_free_and_report_credits_are_not_paying(self):
        self.grant(CreditGrant.FREE, 'free:1')
        self.grant(CreditGrant.REWARD, 'report:1')
        self.assertContains(self.signed_in(), OFFER)

    def test_anyone_who_ever_bought_a_pack_gets_nothing(self):
        self.grant(CreditGrant.PACK, 'inv:1')
        self.assertNoBox(self.signed_in())

    def test_anyone_who_ever_had_a_plan_gets_nothing_after_it_lapsed(self):
        self.grant(CreditGrant.SUBSCRIPTION, 'sub:1')
        JusPrinPlan.objects.create(user=self.user, plan_id='jusprin-hobby-monthly', external_id='x',
                                   external_user_id='y', expired_at=timezone.now() - timedelta(days=1))
        self.assertNoBox(self.signed_in())

    def test_a_subscriber_gets_nothing_before_the_plan_grants_credits(self):
        JusPrinPlan.objects.create(user=self.user, plan_id='jusprin-workshop-monthly', external_id='x',
                                   external_user_id='y')
        self.assertNoBox(self.signed_in())

    def test_a_v1_subscriber_gets_nothing(self):
        JusPrinPlan.objects.create(user=self.user, plan_id='jusprin-unlimited-annual', external_id='x',
                                   external_user_id='y')
        self.assertNoBox(self.signed_in())

    def test_a_token_that_no_longer_works_gets_nothing(self):
        AccessToken.objects.filter(token=self.token).update(expires=timezone.now() - timedelta(seconds=1))
        self.assertNoBox(self.signed_in())

    def test_nobody_gets_the_offer_once_it_ends(self):
        with override_settings(REDACTED.now()):
            self.assertNoBox(Client().get(URL))
            self.assertNoBox(self.signed_in())
        with override_settings(REDACTED.now() + timedelta(minutes=1)):
            self.assertContains(Client().get(URL), SIGN_UP)

    def test_the_box_has_no_script_and_no_link(self):
        # The app's frame runs no scripts and opens no links; neither would work.
        for response in (Client().get(URL), self.signed_in()):
            html = response.content.decode().lower()
            self.assertNotIn('<script', html)
            self.assertNotIn('<a ', html)

# CLAUDE.md - Testing Guide for OrcaSlicer

This guide provides comprehensive instructions for Claude Code when writing, maintaining, and understanding tests in the OrcaSlicer codebase.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - MUST FOLLOW

### 1. **SECTIONS IN LOOPS - NEVER REUSE NAMES**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause unpredictable behavior
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Bad loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development
```bash
# Essential flags for running tests
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# For test sharding (parallel execution), share random seed
./tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
```

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

OrcaSlicer uses **Catch2 v3** (currently v3.11.0, vendored in `tests/catch2/`) as its primary testing framework. The test suite is organized into several modules that mirror the project's architectural components:

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

### Test Structure
```
tests/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Main test configuration
├── catch_main.hpp              # Custom test reporter
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
├── fff_print/                  # FFF printing tests (12 test files)
├── sla_print/                  # SLA printing tests (4 test files)
├── libnest2d/                  # 2D nesting tests
├── slic3rutils/               # Utility tests
├── data/                      # Test data files and meshes
└── catch2/                    # Catch2 framework files
```

### Build Integration
- Tests are built using CMake with `catch_discover_tests()` integration
- Each test module creates a separate executable (e.g., `libslic3r_tests`, `fff_print_tests`)
- Test data directory is available via `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition
- Custom verbose console reporter provides detailed test output

## Test Suite Organization

### libslic3r Tests
Core slicing engine tests covering:
- **Geometry operations**: Points, polygons, lines, Voronoi diagrams
- **File formats**: STL, 3MF, AMF parsing and validation
- **Algorithms**: Clipper operations, mesh boolean operations, optimization
- **Configuration**: Print settings validation and parsing
- **Utilities**: String processing, time utilities, data structures

### fff_print Tests
Fused Filament Fabrication specific tests:
- **G-code generation**: Writer functionality, cooling, lift/unlift
- **Slicing algorithms**: Layer generation, infill patterns
- **Print mechanics**: Flow calculations, extrusion, support material
- **Model processing**: Print objects, skirt/brim generation

### sla_print Tests
Stereolithography specific tests:
- **SLA print processing**: Layer curing, support generation
- **Raycast operations**: Light path calculations
- **Test utilities**: SLA-specific helper functions

## Writing New Tests - Best Practices

### File Organization
1. **Naming Convention**: `test_<feature>.cpp` (e.g., `test_geometry.cpp`)
2. **Header Structure**: Include `<catch2/catch_all.hpp>` first, then relevant headers
3. **Namespace Usage**: Use `using namespace Slic3r;` for convenience
4. **File Placement**: Add to appropriate test directory and update CMakeLists.txt

### Test Naming and Structure
```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>
#include "libslic3r/Point.hpp"

using namespace Slic3r;

TEST_CASE("Feature description", "[category_tag]") {
    // Test implementation
}
```

### Tagging System
Use descriptive tags for test categorization:
- `[Geometry]` - Geometric operations and calculations
- `[GCodeWriter]` - G-code generation functionality  
- `[Config]` - Configuration and settings tests
- `[FileFormat]` - File I/O operations (STL, 3MF, etc.)
- `[Algorithm]` - Core algorithms and processing
- `[Performance]` - Performance benchmarks (if applicable)

## Catch2 Features Guide

### Basic Assertions
```cpp
// Primary assertions - stop test on failure
REQUIRE(expression);
REQUIRE_FALSE(expression);

// Continuing assertions - continue test after failure  
CHECK(expression);
CHECK_FALSE(expression);

// Non-failing checks - record result but don't fail test
CHECK_NOFAIL(expression);  // Useful for assumptions that might be violated
```

### Exception Testing
```cpp
// Verify no exception is thrown
REQUIRE_NOTHROW(function_call());

// Verify any exception is thrown
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());

// Verify specific exception type
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(function_call(), SpecificException);

// Verify exception message
REQUIRE_THROWS_WITH(function_call(), "Expected error message");

// Verify exception with matchers (for partial matching)
REQUIRE_THROWS_MATCHES(function_call(), SpecificException, 
                       Catch::Matchers::Message("contains this"));
```

### Complex Assertions with Matchers
```cpp
#include <catch2/matchers/catch_matchers.hpp>

// String matchers
using Catch::Matchers::StartsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::EndsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring;
using Catch::Matchers::Equals;
using Catch::Matchers::Matches;  // Regex matching

REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, StartsWith("Expected prefix"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, ContainsSubstring("middle part"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, Matches(".*pattern.*"));

// Floating point matchers - ALWAYS use these instead of Approx!
using Catch::Matchers::WithinAbs;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinRel;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinULP;

REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));     // Absolute tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));      // Relative tolerance (1%)
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));         // ULP difference (requires IEEE-754)

// Combining matchers
REQUIRE_THAT(value, WithinRel(expected, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));
```

### Sections for Test Organization
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Complex feature testing", "[Feature]") {
    // Common setup code
    SomeObject obj;
    
    SECTION("First scenario") {
        // Specific test case
        REQUIRE(obj.method1() == expected_value);
    }
    
    SECTION("Second scenario") {
        // Another test case with same setup
        REQUIRE(obj.method2() == other_expected);
    }
}
```

### BDD-Style Tests
Use for complex scenarios and user story testing:

> **Note**: BDD macros are aliases for TEST_CASE and SECTION with prefixed names
```cpp
SCENARIO("User performs complex operation", "[UserStory]") {
    GIVEN("A specific setup condition") {
        GCodeWriter writer;
        // Setup code
        
        WHEN("User performs action") {
            auto result = writer.some_operation();
            
            THEN("Expected outcome occurs") {
                REQUIRE(result.size() > 0);
                
                AND_WHEN("Follow-up action occurs") {
                    auto next_result = writer.next_operation();
                    
                    THEN("Final outcome is correct") {
                        REQUIRE(next_result == expected);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Data Generators for Parameterized Tests
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Function works with various inputs", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto test_value = GENERATE(1, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13);
    
    REQUIRE(is_odd(test_value));
    REQUIRE(test_value > 0);
}

// Range-based generators
TEST_CASE("Range testing", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto i = GENERATE(range(1, 10));  // 1 to 9
    REQUIRE(process_value(i) > i);
}

// Using variables in generators (requires GENERATE_COPY or GENERATE_REF)
TEST_CASE("Generator with variables", "[Algorithm]") {
    std::vector<int> values = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    auto test_value = GENERATE_REF(from_range(values));  // Use GENERATE_REF for references
    
    REQUIRE(test_value > 0);
}

// Custom generators
TEST_CASE("Random values", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto random_int = GENERATE(take(100, random(-1000, 1000)));  // 100 random values
    REQUIRE(process_random_value(random_int));
}
```

### Test Fixtures
```cpp
class GeometryFixture {
public:
    Point origin{0, 0};
    Point unit_x{1, 0};
    Point unit_y{0, 1};
    
    mutable double tolerance = EPSILON;  // Use mutable for data that might change
};

// Standard fixture - new instance per test run
TEST_CASE_METHOD(GeometryFixture, "Point operations", "[Geometry]") {
    REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_x) == 1.0);
}

// Persistent fixture - single instance for entire test case (v3.2.0+)
TEST_CASE_PERSISTENT_FIXTURE(GeometryFixture, "Persistent operations", "[Geometry]") {
    static int call_count = 0;
    ++call_count;
    INFO("This fixture persists across sections, call: " << call_count);
    
    SECTION("First section") {
        REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_x) == 1.0);
    }
    
    SECTION("Second section") {
        REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_y) == 1.0);
        // call_count will be 2 here with persistent fixture
    }
}

// Template fixtures for type-parameterized tests
template<typename T>
class NumericFixture {
public:
    T zero = T{0};
    T one = T{1};
};

TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE_METHOD(NumericFixture, "Numeric operations", "[Template]", int, float, double) {
    REQUIRE(TestType{} == this->zero);
    REQUIRE(TestType{1} == this->one);
}
```

### Advanced Testing Features

#### Logging and Information Macros
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Advanced logging", "[Logging]") {
    INFO("This info persists until end of scope");
    
    SECTION("Section A") {
        INFO("Section A specific info");
        CAPTURE(some_variable, another_var);  // Captures variable names and values
        CHECK(some_condition);
    }
    
    SECTION("Section B") {
        UNSCOPED_INFO("This survives beyond its scope");  // v2.7.0+
        CHECK(other_condition);
    }
}

// Warning and explicit control
TEST_CASE("Explicit test control", "[Control]") {
    WARN("This warns but doesn't fail the test");
    
    if (precondition_not_met) {
        SKIP("Reason");  // Marks the test as skipped (v3.3.0+, available)
        return;
    }
    
    if (critical_failure) {
        FAIL("Critical condition failed");  // Fails and stops test
    }
    
    SUCCEED("Reached successful completion");  // Explicit success marker
}
```

#### Static Assertions (Compile-time Testing)
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Compile-time checks", "[Static]") {
    STATIC_REQUIRE(sizeof(int) >= 4);  // Checked at compile time
    STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE(std::is_void_v<int>);
    
    // For traits and template metaprogramming
    STATIC_CHECK(std::is_trivially_copyable_v<Point>);  // v3.0.1+
}
```

#### Conditional Testing
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Conditional blocks", "[Conditional]") {
    int value = get_test_value();
    
    // These record the expression but don't count as test failures (v3.0.1+)
    CHECKED_IF(value > 0) {
        // This block runs if value > 0
        REQUIRE(value <= 100);
    } CHECKED_ELSE(value > 0) {
        // This block runs if value <= 0  
        REQUIRE(value >= -100);
    }
}
```

#### Benchmarking (v2.9.0+)
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Performance testing", "[Benchmark]") {
    // Simple benchmarking
    BENCHMARK("Algorithm performance") {
        return expensive_algorithm();
    };
    
    // Advanced benchmarking with setup
    BENCHMARK_ADVANCED("Advanced benchmark")(Catch::Benchmark::Chronometer meter) {
        std::vector<int> data = setup_test_data();  // Setup not measured
        
        meter.measure([&] { 
            return process_data(data);  // Only this is measured
        });
    };
}
```

### Geometry Testing
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Line operations", "[Geometry]") {
    Line line{{100000, 0}, {0, 0}};
    Line parallel{{200000, 0}, {0, 0}};
    
    REQUIRE(line.parallel_to(line));
    REQUIRE(line.parallel_to(parallel));
    
    // Test with epsilon tolerance

    rotated.rotate(0.9 * EPSILON, {0, 0});

}

TEST_CASE("Config loading", "[Config]") {

### File I/O Testing
```cpp
TEST_CASE("STL file parsing", "[FileFormat]") {
    std::string stl_path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/test_stl/20mmbox.stl";

    REQUIRE_NOTHROW(mesh.ReadSTLFile(stl_path.c_str()));

### G-code Generation Testing
```cpp
TEST_CASE("G-code writer functionality", "[GCodeWriter]") {
    GCodeWriter writer;
    
    // Load test configuration
    std::string config_path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/fff_print_tests/test_config.ini";
    writer.config.load(config_path, ForwardCompatibilitySubstitutionRule::Disable);
    
    // Test specific G-code generation
    std::string result = writer.lift();

    REQUIRE_THAT(result, Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring("G1"));

### Performance Testing Patterns
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Algorithm performance", "[Performance][Algorithm]") {
    // Large test data
    std::vector<Point> points = generate_large_point_set(10000);
    
    // Time the operation (manual timing example; the BENCHMARK macro is also available)
    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    auto result = convex_hull(points);
    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    
    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);
    
    REQUIRE(result.size() > 0);
    REQUIRE(duration.count() < 1000);  // Should complete in < 1 second
}
```

### Custom String Conversions

#### For Custom Types
```cpp
// Method 1: operator<< overload (preferred)
std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& os, const Point& point) {
    os << "Point(" << point.x << ", " << point.y << ")";
    return os;
}

// Method 2: StringMaker specialization
namespace Catch {
    template<>
    struct StringMaker<MyCustomType> {
        static std::string convert(const MyCustomType& value) {
            return "MyCustomType{" + std::to_string(value.data) + "}";
        }
    };
}

// Method 3: Enum registration (v2.8.0+)
enum class Status { Ready, Processing, Complete, Error };

// Must be at global scope!
CATCH_REGISTER_ENUM(Status, Status::Ready, Status::Processing, Status::Complete, Status::Error);

// Method 4: Exception translation
CATCH_TRANSLATE_EXCEPTION(MyCustomException const& ex) {
    return "MyCustomException: " + std::string(ex.what());
}

// Method 5: Disable range iteration for problematic types
namespace Catch {
    template<>
    struct is_range<ProblematicType> {
        static const bool value = false;
    };
}
```

## Running and Debugging Tests

### Building Tests
```bash
# Build all tests
cd build && make

# Build specific test suite
cd build && make libslic3r_tests

# Build and run tests
cd build && make && ctest
```

### Running Tests

#### Essential Test Execution Patterns
```bash
# REQUIRED: Random order with assertion warnings (best practice)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# Run all tests with verbose output via CTest
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure

# Run specific test suite with best practices
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# Filter tests with specific tags
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests "[Geometry]" --order rand

# Filter by test name patterns
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests "*geometry*" --order rand

# Exclude tests (negation)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests "~[Performance]" --order rand

# Combine filters: (Geometry AND Config) OR Algorithm
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests "[Geometry][Config],[Algorithm]" --order rand

# List available tests, tags, and reporters
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --list-tests
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --list-tags  
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --list-reporters

# Debug failing tests
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --break    # Break into debugger on failure
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --success  # Show passing tests too
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --durations yes  # Show timing info

# Abort on first failure
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --abort

# Test sharding for parallel execution (MUST share random seed)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 3 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &
wait  # Wait for all to complete
```

#### Reporter Options for CI Integration

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

### Memory Management
Use RAII and smart pointers in tests:
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Resource management", "[Memory]") {
    auto model = std::make_unique<Model>();
    // Automatic cleanup on test completion/failure
    
    REQUIRE(model->objects.empty());
}
```

## Performance Considerations

### Compilation Optimizations
```cpp
// In CMakeLists.txt or as preprocessor definition
#define CATCH_CONFIG_FAST_COMPILE  // 20% faster compilation, disables some features

// For faster test iteration during development
#define CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION  // Workaround for VS2017 raw string bug
```

### Runtime Performance
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Performance-sensitive test", "[Performance]") {
    // Manual timing example (Catch2's built-in BENCHMARK macro is also available)
    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    
    auto result = expensive_operation();
    
    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);
    
    REQUIRE(result.is_valid());
    REQUIRE(duration.count() < 1000);  // Should complete in < 1 second
    
    INFO("Operation took " << duration.count() << "ms");
}
```

### Memory Leak Detection
```cpp
// For Windows builds - detects memory leaks
#define CATCH_CONFIG_WINDOWS_CRTDBG  // Must be defined for whole build
```

## Integration with CMake

### Adding New Test Files
1. Create test file: `test_new_feature.cpp`
2. Add to appropriate `CMakeLists.txt`:
```cmake
add_executable(${_TEST_NAME}_tests 
    ${_TEST_NAME}_tests.cpp
    test_existing_feature.cpp
    test_new_feature.cpp  # Add here
)
```

### Advanced Test Discovery
```cmake
# Basic test discovery
catch_discover_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: ")

# Advanced test discovery with customization
catch_discover_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests
    TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: "
    TEST_SUFFIX " (auto)"
    WORKING_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}
    EXTRA_ARGS --order rand --warn NoAssertions
    PROPERTIES 
        TIMEOUT 300
        LABELS "unit;core"
    DISCOVERY_MODE PRE_TEST  # or POST_BUILD
    REPORTER junit
    OUTPUT_DIR ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/test-results
    OUTPUT_PREFIX "results_"
    OUTPUT_SUFFIX ".xml"
)

# Test sharding for parallel execution
include(CatchShardTests)  # If available
catch_shard_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests
    SHARD_COUNT 4
    TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}_shard: "
)
```

### Conditional Test Compilation
```cmake
# Feature-dependent tests
if (TARGET OpenVDB::openvdb)
    target_sources(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE test_hollowing.cpp)
endif()

# Platform-specific tests
if(WIN32)
    target_sources(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE test_windows_specific.cpp)
elseif(UNIX)
    target_sources(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE test_unix_specific.cpp)
endif()

# Compiler-specific workarounds
if(MSVC)
    target_compile_definitions(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION)
endif()

# Fast compile mode for development
if(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE STREQUAL "Debug")
    target_compile_definitions(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE CATCH_CONFIG_FAST_COMPILE)
endif()
```

## Known Issues and Workarounds

### Platform-Specific Issues
```cpp
// MinGW/CygWin slow linking workaround
// Use: -fuse-ld=lld flag to speed up linking significantly

// Visual Studio 2017 raw string literal bug
#define CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION
// This disables expression stringification but works around the compiler bug

// Visual Studio 2022 spaceship operator issue
// REQUIRE((a <=> b) == 0);  // May not compile with MSVC
// Workaround: use clang-cl or avoid spaceship in assertions

// QNX/VxWorks C stdlib issues
#include <cfoo>           // Use C++ headers
std::foo_function();     // Always call qualified
// NOT: #include <foo.h> and foo_function();
```

### Catch2 v3 Features Available
```cpp
// OrcaSlicer is on Catch2 v3.11.0 - all of these ARE available:
// SKIP() macro                           - v3.3.0+
// Opt-in thread-safe assertions          - v3.9.0+ (NOT enabled here; see Thread Safety)
// Built-in BENCHMARK / BENCHMARK_ADVANCED - v3.x
// testCasePartial events                 - v3.0.1+
// Multiple reporters simultaneously      - v3.0.1+
// STATIC_CHECK macro                     - v3.0.1+
// Built-in test sharding (--shard-*)     - v3.x

// v3 notes to remember:
// - String matcher is "ContainsSubstring" (v2's "Contains" no longer exists)
// - Sections can still be re-run if a later section fails (unchanged from v2)
```

### Test Organization Best Practices

#### Project Structure Rules
1. **1:1 correspondence**: One test binary per library/module
2. **Hidden tests**: Use `[.]` or `[!benchmark]` tags for tests that shouldn't run by default
3. **Tag hierarchy**: Use consistent tagging scheme across the project
4. **File naming**: Follow `test_<feature>.cpp` pattern

#### CI/CD Integration
```bash
# Essential CI test command
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --reporter junit::out=results.xml

# For coverage analysis
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --reporter console --success

# For performance tracking
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --durations yes
```

This comprehensive guide ensures robust, maintainable, and efficient testing practices for OrcaSlicer development with Claude Code, incorporating all critical knowledge from the official Catch2 documentation.
